items.title: Ras Kuuku rules out politics over ‘too much hatred’
items.description: For many Ghanaians who have imagined Ras Kuuku in political office, the reggae-dancehall musician has completely ruled out that possibility. In an interview on Joy Prime, Ras Kuuku explained that the level of hostility among politicians is one of the main reasons he has no interest in seeking public office. According to him, politics is usually characterized by a level of animosity and deliberate character smear and propaganda which he finds unattractive. He argued that political opponents often turn against each other despite belonging to the same communities and even worshipping together. “I don’t think there’s anybody who has sat on TV or something and dissed Raskuku. But when it comes to politics, you know there’s hatred. People hate each other too much, and later you see them go to church.” Ras Kuuku specifically pointed to the rivalry between Ghana’s major political parties, the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and the National Democratic Congress (NDC), saying the divisions can follow people even into places of worship. The musician maintained that even if his community approached him to represent them in Parliament, he would still decline because he does not want to become involved in the political environment. His position, however, does not mean he has withdrawn from civic participation. Ras Kuuku said he votes during elections because he wants to be actively involved in the selection of a befitting leader. For Ras Kuuku, therefore, participating in Ghana’s democracy is important, but seeking political office is a line he does not intend to cross.

items.title: I sold pure water, rubber bags – Ras Kuuku recalls life before fame
items.description: Ghanaian reggae-dancehall musician Ras Kuuku has opened up about the difficult beginnings that shaped his life before he found success in music. The musician revealed that he sold pure water, food and rubber bags as a young boy while growing up in Dome, Accra, following the death of his mother at an early age. Shedding more light on his childhood in an interview on Joy Prime, Ras Kuuku, born Kojo Kurankye, said he was raised by his aunt, who despite making him engage in petty trading, ensured that his education remained a priority. He recalled moving from Dome to Nungua Presby where he later continuing his education, while taking on various jobs to support himself. Ras Kuuku also recalled an unusual aspect of his early education, explaining that he skipped some classes before eventually returning to class two so he could be in the same class as his aunt’s son. Despite the difficulties, Ras Kuuku said he never abandoned his ambitions. At the time, his biggest dream was to become a footballer, and he described himself as a talented bowler who took the sport seriously. Music, however, would eventually become the path that changed his fortunes. The young boy who once sold pure water, food and rubber bags in Dome has gone on to build a career in reggae-dancehall and earn recognition as one of Ghana’s notable artistes.

items.title: MTN passes on tax windfall
items.description: When the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) revised Value Added Tax Act took effect on January 1, few consumers would have expected their mobile operator to respond within 24 hours. Yet by the following morning, MTN Ghana — the country’s dominant telecoms operator — had cut tariffs across its entire product suite, from voice calls to data bundles to device financing. The speed of the move was unusual. The economics behind it are more interesting still. Modest tax cut, passed through in full The proximate cause is straightforward. Act 1151 lowered Ghana’s effective VAT rate from 21.9 per cent to 20 per cent, the product of three technical adjustments: the removal of the pandemic-era Health Recovery Levy, the re-coupling of health and education levies into the VAT base to allow input tax credits, and the scrapping of the VAT Flat Rate Scheme. The net effect was a 1.9 percentage point reduction in the tax embedded in the price of everyday services — telecoms among them. MTN’s response was to mirror that reduction almost mechanically. A call tariff of GH¢0.144 a minute on some plans slipped to roughly GH¢0.1421 — hardly the stuff of a rate war, but multiplied across a subscriber base in the tens of millions and billions of daily transactions, the aggregate saving is not trivial. The company confirmed the adjustment took effect from January 2, having run a systems maintenance window overnight to update billing platforms in time. Operationally, this is unremarkable — a large company adjusting prices to reflect a change in tax law, as economic theory would predict in a reasonably competitive market. What makes it worth a second look is the market structure MTN operates within. Significant market player problem In 2020, Ghana’s National Communications Authority designated MTN a “Significant Market Player” — a regulatory classification reserved for operators whose scale gives them outsized influence over sector pricing. At the time, MTN held roughly 57 per cent of the voice market and 68 per cent of mobile data. The SMP status came with obligations, including constraints on certain on-net tariffs, designed to prevent the incumbent from squeezing smaller rivals. Judged by the numbers, those interventions have not much dented MTN’s trajectory. The company’s mobile voice share has since risen to about 72.7 per cent and its data share to roughly 79 per cent, according to the most recent NCA figures — an unusual outcome for a firm operating under pro-competitive constraints, and one that raises a familiar question in telecoms regulation: whether structural remedies aimed at dominant operators are keeping pace with the scale economies that reinforce that dominance in the first place. Journalists for Business Advocacy (JBA) tracking None of this is to suggest MTN’s tariff cut was disingenuous. Independent research from Journalists for Business Advocacy, a network tracking economic reporting in the region, points to MTN being widely regarded as the most cost-competitive operator in the Ghanaian market. But a company can be simultaneously the most price-competitive option available to consumers and the primary beneficiary of a market structure tilted in its favour — the two are not mutually exclusive, and Ghana’s telecoms sector may be a case study in exactly that dynamic. The more consequential story here may not be the tariff reduction itself but what cheaper connectivity does further down the economy. Ghana’s mobile networks are the primary on-ramp to the internet for most citizens; data pricing is, in effect, a proxy for internet accessibility. Sectors built on mobile connectivity — ride-hailing, mobile money, e-commerce, digital media — carry that cost directly into their own margins. For small and medium enterprises operating on thin margins already, marginal reductions in connectivity costs compound: lower data costs support digital adoption, digital adoption supports formalisation, and formalisation is, per MTN’s own stated strategy, a precondition for access to credit that many small operators currently lack. Seen this way, the tariff cut is not simply pass-through economics — it is one input into a broader corporate strategy in which MTN positions affordable connectivity as the foundation for a wider ecosystem of financial inclusion and enterprise growth in Ghana, an ecosystem in which MTN itself sits as intermediary. Regulatory question The swiftness of MTN’s response to the VAT reform is likely to be cited favourably by the company and, potentially, by policymakers keen to demonstrate that fiscal reforms translate into consumer benefit. Fair enough, as far as it goes. But regulators assessing whether Ghana’s telecoms market remains genuinely contestable will need to look past a single well-timed tariff adjustment and toward the more persistent trend beneath it: an operator that, despite years of SMP-related constraints, has continued to consolidate rather than cede market share. For consumers, this week’s price cuts are an unambiguous, if modest, gain. For the National Communications Authority, this is a reminder that pricing behaviour and market structure are separate questions — and that the first can look benign even as the second continues to move in a direction the SMP framework was designed to prevent.

items.title: FCSC begins online accreditation for promotion exercise
items.description: By Favour Ulebor The Federal Civil Service Commission (FCSC) has commenced the online accreditation exercise for officers on Salary Grade Levels 14, 15 and 16 participating in the 2026 promotion exercise. In a statement on Thursday, signed by the Head of Press and Public Relations, Mr. Ibraheem Zakariyya, the Commission said affected officers are expected to complete their accreditation through the designated promotion portal between August 14 and August 28, 2026. According to the statement, the directive was issued by the Chairman of the Commission as part of efforts to ensure a transparent, orderly and timely promotion exercise. The Commission explained that candidates would access the portal using login details to be sent to their registered email addresses and urged them to complete the process within the stipulated period. It warned that the accreditation portal would close on August 28 and that no extension would be granted. According to the Commission, officers who fail to complete the exercise within the deadline would be required to re-present themselves for accreditation in 2027. The FCSC also advised candidates not to wait until the closing date before carrying out the accreditation process to avoid any challenges that may arise. The Commission further directed Permanent Secretaries, Accounting Officers and Chief Executive Officers of Ministries, Departments and Agencies to ensure that all eligible officers, including those serving within and outside their headquarters as well as those on foreign assignments, are informed of the exercise for compliance. items.title: Kennedy Center board votes to restore Trump name – Reports
items.description: US President Donald Trump has sought to burnish his legacy by getting his name and image placed on everything, from limited edition passports to a Florida airport. His efforts to put his stamp on the Kennedy Center arts complex in Washington — blocked earlier this year by a federal judge — moved ahead once again on Thursday. The venue’s board of trustees, which is stacked with Trump allies, reportedly voted to approve a workaround by adding the inscription “Restored and Renovated by President Donald J. Trump” to the building. The New York Times and The Washington Post, citing unnamed sources with knowledge of the proceedings, said the inscription would go directly below the main signage. It was not immediately clear how the decision would comply with a federal judge’s order in May that Trump’s name be removed from the facade, as only Congress can change it. In mid-June, the center’s Executive Director Matt Floca said it had “removed all physical signage on the Kennedy Center building and grounds” containing Trump’s name. But a tarp has remained over the facade since that time, sparking questions about the actual changes. On Thursday, the board also voted to close the center’s main building for two years for renovations. Work on the venue’s heating and cooling, electrical and fire safety systems is to be completed by summer 2028. A judge had also blocked that plan, but said it could be reconsidered after further review. The Kennedy Center did not immediately reply to AFP’s request for comment on the board’s proceedings. Since returning to the White House in January 2025, former reality TV star Trump has aggressively imprinted his personal brand on institutions, eschewing political tradition. The Kennedy Center’s board initially voted in December to rename the venue as “The Donald J. Trump and John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts.” The Republican president’s name was quickly added to the facade in large letters above that of Kennedy, spurring the cancellation of shows and plunging ticket sales for remaining events. Elsewhere in Washington, the now-defunct US Institute of Peace was also renamed after Trump, and his face has stared down from huge banners hung outside the Justice and Agriculture Departments. His image is featured on a limited edition US passport, and the airport in West Palm Beach, Florida is now named for him. items.title: MTN’s long game on small business, A JBA analysis
items.description: For the roadside seamstress balancing a ledger she keeps by hand, or the young entrepreneur selling handmade goods with no collateral to show a bank, the promise of growth in Ghana has long collided with a familiar obstacle: the absence of paperwork, capital and connectivity that formal institutions demand. It is these small and medium-sized enterprises — the shopkeepers, tailors, food vendors and tech tinkerers who make up the bulk of commercial activity in the country’s economy — whose fortunes now sit at the centre of a fresh push by MTN Ghana. MTN Ghana this week unveiled the third edition of its SME Accelerate programme, a year-long campaign of training, digital-tool subsidies and market access initiatives designed to pull small businesses further into the formal economy. The launch, held at the company’s Accra headquarters, doubles as a bet that closing the digital divide for millions of small operators is not just good citizenship, but good business. The Journalists for Business Advocacy (JBA) were present at the launch. What distinguishes this year’s iteration is the breadth of MTN’s direct involvement — not simply as a sponsor lending its name, but as an operator building products, financing partnerships and setting multiyear targets around a segment of the economy it has historically treated as a secondary market. Anatomy of MTN’s support The centerpiece of MTN’s contribution is Yellow Biz, a bundled package that gives small business owners internet connectivity, a business email address and a website, priced below what most owners could otherwise assemble by purchasing each service separately. For an operator with no formal online presence, this is the difference between existing solely as a market stall and having a discoverable, transactable storefront. MTN also runs Ajumapa , a product line aimed specifically at women-owned businesses, extending the company’s digital-inclusion push into a demographic that studies across the region consistently show has less access to formal financial and digital services than male-owned firms. Credit-readiness coaching MTN’s leadership has been candid that connectivity alone does not solve small businesses’ biggest constraint: capital. Chief Enterprise Business Officer Angela Mensah-Poku described banks routinely turning away owners who lack formal assets or documentation, unwilling to accept an informal ledger as evidence of creditworthiness. Rather than lending directly, MTN’s role here is preparatory — helping businesses build the certification, transaction records and formal structure that lenders require, effectively positioning the telecom as an intermediary that manufactures “bankability” where none previously existed. This is a notable expansion of MTN’s remit, moving the company from connectivity provider toward something closer to a financial-inclusion enabler. Training and certification at national scale Unlike a one-off workshop or regional pilot, SME Accelerate is structured to reach every region of the country over a full year, combining training sessions with formal certification — a credential system intended to give small operators something to show partners, lenders and customers alike. MTN is also organizing fairs where SMEs can showcase goods directly to consumers, a lower-cost, higher-trust alternative to digital advertising for businesses without a marketing budget. This gives participants a tangible, near-term benefit — foot traffic and sales — even before the longer-term digital and credit benefits materialize. MTN is not underwriting the initiative alone. It has brought in Mastercard, whose participation suggests a payments and financial-inclusion component beyond what MTN’s own products cover, and GIZ, Germany’s development agency, which typically contributes technical assistance and funding aligned with donor-backed enterprise development goals. Government stakeholders focused on youth employment round out the coalition. This partner mix indicates MTN is positioning itself as the convening organizer of a broader public-private effort rather than the sole financier — spreading cost and lending third-party credibility to the program’s outcomes. Multiyear commitment Company leadership was explicit in framing SME Accelerate as an ongoing institutional priority rather than a marketing cycle: Mensah-Poku described MTN’s commitment as extending across the next several years, explicitly rejecting the idea that this was a one-time initiative the company would abandon once attention moved elsewhere. That this is the third consecutive year of the program lends some credibility to the claim — it suggests a standing internal budget and team rather than an ad hoc announcement. Why it matters Small and medium-sized enterprises are widely regarded as the primary engine of employment and economic activity across Ghana and much of Sub-Saharan Africa. Initiatives like this one test a proposition with implications well beyond one company’s balance sheet: that the fastest way to grow a consumer base and a data-driven economy is to first make small businesses bankable. Whether MTN’s approach meaningfully narrows the financing gap — or simply deepens small businesses’ dependence on a single corporate ecosystem — will likely become clearer as the program moves through its promised decade-long run.

items.title: Large-scale miners commit 30% of gold output to BoG, GoldBod under GANRAP
items.description: Government has reached an agreement with Ghana’s large-scale mining companies to implement a key component of the Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Programme (GANRAP), requiring 30% of their gold output to be sold to the Bank of Ghana (BoG) and the Ghana Gold Board for local processing and refining. The agreement was formalised on Thursday through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, Bank of Ghana, Ghana Gold Board and Ghana Chamber of Mines, which represented the country’s large-scale mining companies. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson said the agreement followed extensive consultations among government, the Chamber of Mines, mining companies, the central bank and the Gold Board. He said the signing marked the conclusion of negotiations on the implementation of the 30% gold purchase component of GANRAP. “Today’s signing of the memorandum of understanding signifies that we have successfully come to a mutual understanding that that policy will be implemented effective the date of signing,” Dr Ato Forson said. Under the arrangement, gold purchased from large-scale mining companies will be processed and refined locally before being transferred to the Bank of Ghana to support the country’s reserve accumulation efforts. Dr Ato Forson said the agreement represents a major step in Government’s efforts to strengthen Ghana’s reserve position and promote macroeconomic stability.

items.title: Investigate Mahama relative’s alleged role in AKSA deal – Manhyia South MP
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Manhyia South, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, has called for a thorough investigation into the alleged involvement of a relative of President John Dramani Mahama in the AKSA Energy power project. Mr Awuah said investigators must establish the identity of the person described in United States court proceedings as a relative of then-President Mahama, as well as the individual’s alleged role in the transaction. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Thursday, August 13, he said the investigation should determine the nature of the person’s relationship with President Mahama, the company or entity with which the individual was associated, and whether the person played any role in the approval of the AKSA project. “The Ghanaian public deserves to know who this person was. What was the person’s relationship with President John Dramani Mahama? What company or entity was the person associated with? What role did the person play in the AKSA transaction?” he asked. The NPP MP further demanded clarification on whether the alleged relative received any payment in connection with the transaction. “If the person received money, how much did the person receive and for what purpose?” he asked. According to Mr Awuah, answering these questions is necessary to determine whether the alleged individual had any financial interest in the AKSA deal or exercised influence over the project’s approval. He said the issue raised concerns similar to those surrounding the Airbus controversy, where a person described in court records as a close relative of a high-ranking Ghanaian official featured in proceedings. Mr Awuah therefore called for the matter to be investigated based on evidence rather than political affiliation. His comments come amid renewed scrutiny of the AKSA Energy power project following the conviction in the United States of former Goldman Sachs banker and former Tema Oil Refinery Managing Director Asante Kwaku Berko in a bribery and money-laundering case linked to the project.

items.title: Ghana can become West Africa’s gold refining hub with right incentives — Chamber of Mines
items.description: The Ghana Chamber of Mines has backed the objectives of the Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Programme (GANRAP), but has called for the initiative to evolve into an incentive-based system that promotes long-term local gold processing and refining. Chief Executive Officer of the Chamber of Mines, Eric Asubonteng, said the mining industry supports GANRAP’s focus on strengthening Ghana’s macroeconomic resilience and building a reserve buffer capable of helping the country withstand external economic shocks. Speaking at the signing of an MoU between Government and large-scale mining companies on the implementation of the programme, Mr Asubonteng also welcomed plans to establish internationally accredited gold refineries in Ghana. He disclosed that the Chamber had already begun exploring opportunities to support local gold refining, including engagements with refineries in Ghana and South Africa. However, he argued that the policy should go beyond its current timeframe and introduce incentives to encourage companies to process and refine gold locally. “We need to look at GANRAP beyond even 2028,” he said, citing countries such as Tanzania, India and South Africa, where incentives are used to promote local beneficiation of minerals. Mr Asubonteng said an incentive-driven approach could position Ghana as a major gold refining hub for West Africa, leveraging the large volumes of gold produced locally and in neighbouring countries. He added that the Chamber would continue working with Government and other stakeholders to address implementation challenges while supporting the broader objectives of GANRAP.

items.title: GHS receives emergency health kits, 600 cholera tests after June floods
items.description: Six Emergency Health Kits and 600 cholera Rapid Diagnostic Tests have been handed over to the Ghana Health Service (GHS) to strengthen the country’s public health response following the floods recorded in June 2026. The support is intended to enhance healthcare delivery and improve disease surveillance in communities affected by the floods, particularly amid concerns over the potential emergence and spread of waterborne diseases. The emergency supplies will provide health workers with additional tools to identify suspected cholera cases and respond promptly to potential outbreaks. The intervention is also expected to support ongoing surveillance and strengthen preparedness at the community level. The initiative forms part of efforts to mitigate the health consequences of the June floods and ensure that affected populations have access to timely healthcare and effective disease prevention measures.

items.title: Gamou 2026 : Tivaouane explore les défis de l’IA et du numérique
items.description: L’intelligence artificielle et les mutations numériques occuperont une place importante dans le programme du Gamou 2026 à Tivaouane, où plusieurs initiatives seront consacrées aux usages, aux enjeux éthiques et aux défis liés à ces nouvelles technologies. Prévue du 16 au 28 août, l’édition 2026 du Mawlid An Nabi est placée sous le thème « Ensemble, penser et agir par le verbe de l’unicité (Tawhid) ». Elle entend notamment articuler réflexion spirituelle et réponses aux mutations du monde contemporain. Un forum consacré à l’intelligence artificielle réunira chercheurs, ingénieurs et guides religieux pour réfléchir aux enjeux liés au développement de cette technologie. Les échanges porteront notamment sur les conditions d’un usage éthique de l’IA et sur la manière d’appréhender ces mutations à partir d’une perspective islamique et sénégalaise. Cette réflexion sera prolongée par plusieurs initiatives numériques. La quatrième édition du Hackathon national du Gamou mobilisera de jeunes développeurs et créateurs autour de solutions numériques destinées aux communautés et à la valorisation de l’héritage spirituel. L’initiative « Sokhna Digital », organisée en partenariat avec Orange Digital Center, mettra également l’accent sur l’inclusion numérique des femmes, avec des formations pratiques consacrées à l’intelligence artificielle et aux outils no-code. Le Salon international du livre islamique et des manuscrits de Tivaouane (Silmit), dont le Maroc sera l’invité d’honneur, abordera pour sa part les enjeux de conservation et de diffusion des manuscrits africains à l’ère du numérique. Chercheurs, oulémas et acteurs du numérique sont attendus autour de ces questions. Salla GUEYE

items.description: Attorney General and Minister for Justice, Dr Dominic Ayine, has questioned the approach adopted in the construction of the National Cathedral, saying the project should not have been handled in the manner it was pursued. Dr Ayine said the expenditure on the controversial project could have been put to other uses, including completing some hospitals under the Agenda 111 programme. Speaking at the district launch of the Free Primary Health Care programme in Bolga East, he said a PwC report on the National Cathedral was presented to him last Friday and had informed his assessment of the project. “The monies spent on the National Cathedral from that Report could have been used to complete some Agenda 111 Hospitals,” Dr Ayine said. He was speaking during President John Dramani Mahama’s two-day “Resetting Ghana Tour” of the Upper East Region when he made the broader criticism, stating: “You don’t build a house of God in the manner in which they went about it.”

items.title: Lands Minister urges flexibility as as Ghana begins 30% gold purchase under GANRAP
items.description: Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, has called for continued cooperation and flexibility among stakeholders as Ghana begins implementing the 30% gold purchase component of the Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Programme (GANRAP). The Minister said the programme could have significant implications for Ghana’s macroeconomic stability and financial management, following the signing of an MoU between Government, the Bank of Ghana, Ghana Gold Board and the Ghana Chamber of Mines. Under the agreement, large-scale mining companies will sell 30% of their gold output to the Bank of Ghana and Gold Board for local processing and refining before the refined gold is transferred to the central bank as part of efforts to build the country’s reserves. Mr Buah commended the Chamber of Mines and large-scale mining companies for their cooperation throughout negotiations leading to the agreement. He assured the mining industry that his Ministry would continue engaging stakeholders to address any challenges that may arise during implementation. He stressed the need for flexibility as the arrangement takes effect, noting that emerging concerns must be resolved through collaboration in a manner that protects the national interest. Meanwhile, Bank of Ghana Governor Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama has pledged the central bank’s support for the successful implementation of the programme. He said the BoG would work with all stakeholders to ensure that GANRAP delivers maximum benefits to the Ghanaian economy.

items.title: GPHA engages freight forwarders to improve cargo movement through Ghana’s ports
items.description: The Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) has engaged freight forwarders and other key industry stakeholders on measures to improve operational efficiency and ensure the smooth movement of cargo through Ghana’s ports. The meeting, led by GPHA Director General, Major General Paul Seidu Tanye-Kulono, focused on practical and sustainable measures to address operational challenges and strengthen collaboration among players in the port and shipping industry. Major General Tanye-Kulono highlighted initiatives being implemented by the Port Authority to improve efficiency and facilitate the movement of cargo. He stressed the importance of closer collaboration with industry stakeholders in identifying challenges and developing sustainable solutions to improve port operations. Stakeholders welcomed the engagement and commended GPHA management for creating a platform for dialogue with industry players. They pledged their support towards efforts to create a more efficient port operating environment and improve trade facilitation. The meeting was attended by representatives from the Ghana Shippers’ Authority, Meridian Port Services, Ghana Institute of Freight Forwarders, Association of Customs House Agents Ghana, Customs Brokers Association of Ghana and Freight Forwarders Association of Ghana. GPHA said it would continue to prioritise partnerships with stakeholders as part of efforts to enhance port efficiency, address operational bottlenecks and facilitate seamless cargo movement.

items.title: Police clarify Labone shootout, say syndicate planned attacks on three banks
items.description: The Ghana Police Service has clarified that Thursday’s security operation at Labone in Accra was triggered by intelligence about a planned robbery targeting three banks in the area. According to the Police, a robbery syndicate was preparing to attack GCB Bank, Ecobank and Zenith Bank when officers moved in to foil the operation. The clarification follows an earlier statement from the Service which indicated that an attempted robbery at the GCB Bank Labone branch had been foiled, with two suspects killed and another arrested. GCB Bank subsequently denied that an attempted robbery had taken place at its Labone branch, stating that the facility was never breached and that no staff, customer, funds or property was affected. In its latest update issued on Thursday, August 13, the Police said it received intelligence at about 10:45am that the suspected gang was preparing to attack the three banks. A police team was immediately deployed to the area, where officers spotted the suspects in two vehicles parked near the banks. One of the vehicles reportedly sped away after the occupants noticed the Police. Officers pursued the vehicle and arrested one suspect, identified as Augustine Okechuku Maazi, while another occupant escaped. The occupants of the second vehicle also attempted to flee and allegedly opened fire at the pursuing officers. The Police returned fire, resulting in the deaths of two suspects. Two vehicles were recovered during the operation — a Toyota Highlander with registration number GS-1434-18 and a Hyundai Tucson with registration number GS-7915-17. The Police also recovered a blow pistol. Augustine Okechuku Maazi remains in police custody and is assisting with investigations as the Service works to establish the full circumstances surrounding the planned robbery and identify other members of the suspected syndicate.

items.title: Alger : mort d’un supporter du CRB, les autorités s’attaquent aux fresques des ultras
items.description: C’est un phénomène qui semble préoccuper les autorités à quelques jours du début du championnat d’ Algérie de Ligue 1 le 27 août prochain : la rivalité entre certains groupes de supporters des équipes de football, communément appelés les « ultras ». Lundi dernier, un drame a en effet secoué le quartier de Diar El Mahçoul, à El Madania, sur les hauteurs d’Alger. Un jeune supporter du CRB mortellement poignardé lors d’une rixe à Alger Un jeune supporter du CR Belouizdad, âgé de 19 ans, a été mortellement poignardé à la suite d’une rixe entre groupes rivaux. Selon les informations rapportées par le quotidien El Khabar , le drame serait parti d’un conflit autour d’une fresque murale réalisée par un groupe d’ultras dans un quartier d’El Madania. Un autre groupe, affilié à un club rival, aurait entrepris de la dégrader, estimant que le quartier constituait son territoire. En représailles, le premier groupe aurait à son tour dégradé une autre fresque, faisant monter la tension entre les deux camps. Le journal ne précise pas l’identité du club rival, mais il s’agirait, selon toute vraisemblance, du Mouloudia d’Alger. La situation a finalement dégénéré en affrontement direct entre les deux groupes. Au cours de la rixe, un jeune supporter du CRB, a reçu un coup de couteau à la cuisse. Grièvement blessé, il a succombé à une importante hémorragie, souligne la même source. Le jeune homme a été inhumé mardi au cimetière d’El Madania, en présence de sa famille, de ses proches et d’un important dispositif de sécurité. Les services de police ont ouvert une enquête afin d’établir les circonstances exactes du drame et d’identifier les responsables, ajoute le journal. Sidi M’hamed lance une opération d’effacement des fresques murales Au lendemain de cette tragédie, les autorités ont décidé de prendre les premières mesures. Les services de la wilaya déléguée de Sidi M’hamed ont en effet entamé une opération visant à enlever et recouvrir de peinture les fresques et autres dessins muraux, ainsi que les drapeaux et fanions des clubs de football présents dans les quartiers relevant de son territoire. « La décision a été prise sur instruction du wali délégué », selon une source informée citée par le même média. L’opération ne devrait toutefois pas se limiter à Sidi M’hamed. Elle devrait s’étendre prochainement à d’autres quartiers et communes de la capitale. Selon cette source, cette première mesure pourrait être suivie d’autres dispositions, plus fermes, destinées à lutter contre les manifestations de « fanatisme et d’extrémisme » liées à certains groupes d’ultras. Les autorités s’interrogent également sur les moyens dont disposent certains de ces groupes et, surtout, sur leurs sources de financement. Le phénomène n’est pourtant pas nouveau. Depuis quelques années, à l’approche de certains matchs considérés comme décisifs ou particulièrement importants, de nombreux quartiers d’Alger ou d’autres wilayas comptant des clubs rivaux se parent des couleurs des clubs. Des quartiers aux couleurs des clubs de football Fresques monumentales, banderoles, drapeaux et autres décorations envahissent les rues. Dans certains quartiers, des immeubles entiers ont même été repeints aux couleurs des équipes locales, donnant parfois à certains espaces urbains l’allure de véritables territoires appartenant aux clubs et à leurs supporters. Cette mobilisation spectaculaire autour des équipes témoigne de la puissance du mouvement des ultras et de leur capacité à organiser des opérations d’envergure. Le sacre du Mouloudia Club d’Alger en championnat d’Algérie l’été dernier en a fourni une nouvelle illustration. Les festivités organisées à cette occasion, notamment le spectaculaire feu d’artifice qui a illuminé Alger et été relayé par des médias du monde entier, ont suscité l’admiration de nombreux Algérois. Mais elles ont également attiré l’attention et suscité la curiosité sur les capacités d’organisation de ces groupes et, par conséquent, sur les moyens financiers nécessaires à la mise en place de telles manifestations. items.title: AG has established a seperate justice system for NDC members – Manhyia South MP alleges
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Manhyia South, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, has accused the Attorney General and Minister for Justice, Dr Dominic Ayine, of creating what he described as a “separate justice system” for members and associates of the National Democratic Congress (NDC). According to the New Patriotic Party (NPP) MP, a series of decisions by the Attorney General to discontinue prosecutions involving individuals associated with the NDC government has raised serious concerns about selective accountability. Mr Awuah was responding to the NDC’s dismissal of the NPP’s concerns over the Attorney General’s handling of cases involving politically exposed persons linked to the governing party. He said the Attorney General’s decision to file nolle prosequi applications in some cases involving former NDC appointees and senior party members had undermined public confidence in his ability to independently investigate and prosecute allegations involving politically connected persons. “We now have an Attorney General who has established a separate justice system for members of the NDC,” he alleged. Mr Awuah also questioned the Attorney General’s justification for discontinuing some cases on the grounds that they had remained before the courts for several years. He argued that the mere length of time a case had spent in court could not, on its own, constitute sufficient grounds for discontinuing a prosecution. He further criticised the Attorney General over the handling of the Unibank case, particularly his refusal, according to Mr Awuah, to provide Parliament with details of a proposed plea bargain involving the accused persons. The MP said the lack of transparency in such matters made it difficult for the public to have confidence in the Attorney General when dealing with cases involving members or associates of the governing NDC. Mr Awuah said the NPP was therefore calling for investigations into the allegations to be conducted strictly on the basis of evidence rather than political affiliation. He also demanded clarification over the identity and alleged role of a person described in United States court proceedings as a relative of then-President John Dramani Mahama in connection with the AKSA Energy deal. According to him, investigators must establish the identity of the individual, the nature of the person’s relationship with President Mahama, the company or entity with which the individual was associated, and the role allegedly played in the AKSA transaction. He also wants investigators to determine whether the individual received any payment and, if so, how much and for what purpose. “The Ghanaian public deserves to know who this person was. What was the person’s relationship with President John Dramani Mahama? What company or entity was the person associated with? What role did the person play in the AKSA transaction?” he asked. Mr Awuah said the questions were particularly important given similarities he drew between the AKSA matter and the Airbus controversy, in which court records also referred to a person described as a relative of a senior Ghanaian official. The Manhyia South MP argued that the investigation should determine whether the alleged relative’s involvement had any influence on the approval process for the AKSA project. His comments come amid renewed scrutiny of the AKSA Energy power project following the conviction in the United States of former Goldman Sachs banker and former Tema Oil Refinery Managing Director Asante Kwaku Berko in a bribery and money-laundering case linked to the project. According to the NPP, it has no confidence in the Attorney General to independently investigate or prosecute persons implicated in the latest bribery allegations surrounding the AKSA Energy power project. The party argues that the investigation must be conducted in a manner that inspires public confidence, particularly because some of the persons who could come under scrutiny are allegedly politically connected to NDC.

items.title: Festival des Plages Maroc Telecom : Al Hoceima vibre au rythme de la musique
items.description: Après M’diq et Tanger, le Festival des Plages Maroc Telecom a posé ses valises à Al Hoceima le 12 août. Pour cette troisième étape, la ville a accueilli un public venu des quatre coins du Maroc, mais aussi de la diaspora marocaine, dans une ambiance festive placée sous le signe de la musique et du partage. Al Hoceima a donné, mercredi 12 août, le coup d’envoi de la troisième étape du Festival des Plages Maroc Telecom. Après les rendez-vous de M’diq et Tanger, la caravane musicale poursuit son parcours estival avec une nouvelle escale dans la ville du Rif. Dès la première soirée, le public était au rendez-vous. La scène d’Al Hoceima a notamment accueilli un artiste originaire de la région, un choix qui a permis de mettre immédiatement en lumière les talents locaux et la richesse du patrimoine artistique de la ville. Cette première soirée s’est déroulée dans une ambiance particulièrement festive. De nombreux spectateurs ont fait le déplacement pour profiter de ce rendez-vous musical gratuit. Le public était composé de personnes venues de différentes régions du Royaume, mais également de nombreux Marocains résidant à l’étranger, actuellement en vacances à Al Hoceima et dans les villes et localités voisines. Cette forte présence témoigne de l’attractivité de la ville durant la saison estivale et de la capacité du Festival des Plages Maroc Telecom à réunir un public particulièrement diversifié autour de la musique. Pour cette nouvelle étape, le Festival a choisi de commencer par un artiste originaire de la région. Une manière de donner une place particulière à la scène artistique locale et de valoriser les talents du territoire. Ce choix s’inscrit dans l’esprit du Festival, qui entend faire vivre les différentes villes accueillant ses scènes tout en offrant une programmation réunissant des artistes issus de différentes régions du Maroc. L’ouverture d’Al Hoceima prend ainsi une dimension particulière : la fête commence avec les talents du territoire avant de laisser place à une programmation destinée à attirer un public toujours plus large. Le Festival des Plages Maroc Telecom restera à Al Hoceima jusqu’au 21 août, avec plusieurs soirées musicales au programme. L’objectif reste le même : proposer au public marocain des concerts gratuits et accessibles à tous, tout en contribuant à l’animation culturelle et touristique des villes côtières qui accueillent les différentes étapes du Festival. Après Al Hoceima, une nouvelle escale se prépare également à Saïdia, où la scène ouvrira ses portes au public à partir du 15 août. items.title: Iran : des responsables de l’administration Trump jugent la situation sans issue et s’inquiètent de l’absence de stratégie
items.description: Des responsables americains s'inquietent de l'absence de strategie claire de l'administration de Donald Trump face a l'Iran, alors que la Maison Blanche peine toujours a definir ce qui pourrait constituer une victoire, rapporte Politico ce 13 août. Plusieurs responsables actuels et anciens decrivent une situation particulierement dangereuse, dans laquelle Washington ne disposerait desormais que d'options difficiles. Le malaise est ouvertement exprime au sein de l'appareil americain. Un responsable connaissant la strategie de l'administration au Moyen-Orient a confie a Politico ne pas voir « de sortie » a la situation actuelle. Dan Shapiro, ancien haut responsable du Pentagone sous Joe Biden, estime pour sa part que Washington s'est place dans un « cul-de-sac » ou il ne reste que de mauvaises options. Ces inquietudes interviennent alors que les objectifs americains ont sensiblement evolue depuis le debut des hostilites. Donald Trump entendait initialement mettre fin au programme nucleaire iranien et detruire une part importante des capacites militaires du pays, tout en laissant planer la possibilite d'un changement de regime a Teheran. Desormais, l'administration americaine semble surtout chercher a obtenir la reouverture complete du detroit d'Ormuz, dont les perturbations affectent le commerce mondial et les marches energetiques. Le debat ne porte donc plus seulement sur les moyens employes contre Teheran, mais aussi sur le resultat que Washington cherche reellement a obtenir. Selon le responsable americain, cite par Politico , l'equipe de Donald Trump comprend fondamentalement mal les dirigeants iraniens et a longtemps parie sur le fait qu'une pression croissante finirait par faire ceder Teheran. Elliott Abrams, ancien conseiller de Donald Trump pour le Moyen-Orient, a de son cote qualifie la situation d'extremement dangereuse et estime que l'administration faisait preuve d'incompetence. Le conflit pese egalement sur les moyens militaires americains. Le quotidien americain The Washington Post estime que les etats-Unis ont perdu environ 25 % de leur flotte de drones lourds MQ-9 Reaper depuis le debut de la guerre, soit au moins 45 appareils. Les pertes representeraient plus de 1,3 milliard de dollars, alors que ces drones sont utilises aussi bien pour des missions de renseignement que pour des frappes. Le media etablit un parallele avec les annees les plus difficiles de la guerre en Irak, lorsque Washington peinait a definir une voie de sortie. L'Iran represente toutefois un defi different : le pays est plus vaste, son gouvernement reste en place, les etats-Unis n'y disposent pas de forces terrestres et les consequences du conflit depassent largement ses frontieres. Trois options sur la table, aucune sans risque Trois grandes orientations sont desormais debattues dans les milieux politiques et strategiques americains, sans qu'aucune n'offre de garantie de succes. La premiere consiste a intensifier la pression militaire. Parmi les propositions rapportees figurent une prise de controle americaine de l'île iranienne de Kharg, davantage d'operations israeliennes visant des dirigeants iraniens, un soutien a certains groupes ethniques a l'interieur du pays et l'encouragement des emirats arabes unis a s'emparer de trois îles disputees avec Teheran. Certains estiment egalement que deux semaines supplementaires de bombardements pourraient suffire a faire ceder l'Iran. Une telle escalade ne garantirait pourtant pas le resultat recherche. Le pouvoir iranien reste profondement implante dans le pays et le sentiment national pourrait renforcer la resistance face aux tentatives visant a exploiter ses divisions internes. Un deuxieme courant plaide au contraire pour une desescalade et une reprise des negociations, quitte a consentir des concessions americaines sur les sanctions. Ses partisans preconisent un accord avec Teheran ou, a defaut, un retrait des etats-Unis du conflit. Ils estiment que l'affaiblissement deja subi par les capacites militaires iraniennes permettrait a Washington de limiter ses pertes sans presenter son intervention comme un echec total. Jennifer Kavanagh, du centre de reflexion Defense Priorities, appelle ainsi les etats-Unis a mettre fin a l'escalade et a repenser leur strategie de defense. La troisieme option repose sur une pression economique et maritime prolongee : maintien du blocus du trafic iranien et renforcement des sanctions dans l'espoir d'obtenir des concessions de Teheran ou de fragiliser les autorites. Son efficacite reste incertaine. Un responsable americain cite par Politico rappelle que Washington estime depuis des decennies que l'economie iranienne se trouve au bord de l'effondrement, sans que cette prevision se soit concretisee. Teheran pourrait en outre maintenir ses restrictions dans le detroit d'Ormuz tant que les etats-Unis bloqueront les navires iraniens, faisant peser une partie du coût economique du bras de fer sur le reste du monde. Le detroit d'Ormuz devient la priorite de Washington La Maison Blanche semble desormais privilegier une pression prolongee plutot qu'une nouvelle escalade immediate. Le magazine americain The Atlantic rapporte qu'apres des bombardements limites et des menaces qui n'ont pas produit les resultats recherches, Washington mise davantage sur les sanctions financieres et le blocus maritime des ports iraniens. Cette strategie pourrait toutefois prendre du temps, alors que l'economie iranienne a montre une capacite de resistance susceptible de compliquer les calculs americains. Le quotidien americain The Wall Street Journal a rapporte que Donald Trump avait envisage de presenter la reouverture complete du detroit d'Ormuz comme une victoire permettant aux etats-Unis de mettre fin au conflit, meme sans nouvel accord sur le programme nucleaire iranien. Ce changement traduit un resserrement sensible des objectifs americains, desormais davantage centres sur le detroit d'Ormuz. La Maison Blanche assure neanmoins que Donald Trump continue de privilegier une solution negociee tout en conservant l'ensemble des options disponibles. Washington et Teheran ont egalement tente ces dernieres semaines, avec l'aide de mediateurs du Moyen-Orient, de definir les conditions d'un nouvel arrangement. Pour l'heure, aucun consensus ne s'est impose a Washington. La difficulte centrale reste donc la meme : determiner quel resultat permettrait aux etats-Unis d'affirmer qu'ils ont atteint leurs objectifs et de mettre un terme aux operations.

items.title: Estados Unidos prevé ejecutar en un solo día a tres personas por primera vez desde 2010
items.description: Estados Unidos se acerca este jueves a un récord sangriento. Para este día están previstas tres ejecuciones en los Estados de Oklahoma, Tennessee y Alabama. La primera de ellas —la que afecta a Carlos Cuesta-Rodriguez, condenado por matar a su novia en 2005— ya se ha producido. Si las otras dos también terminan por celebrarse, será la primera vez en 16 años en la que en un mismo día se ejecuta a tres personas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: GRA Commissioner-General commends Customs for improved revenue performance
items.description: Commissioner-General of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) has commended the Customs Division for its steady improvement in revenue performance in recent months, attributing the gains to the commitment and hard work of officers. He said the progress recorded so far reflects stronger coordination and collaboration across the Division and urged Customs leadership to sustain the momentum as the Authority works towards achieving its end-of-year revenue target. The Commissioner-General encouraged officers and managers to maintain the spirit of teamwork that has contributed to the improved performance while remaining focused on delivering the Authority’s revenue objectives. He, however, stressed that the gains must be matched by discipline, professionalism and ethical conduct. According to him, sustained revenue performance must go hand in hand with protecting the integrity of the GRA and strengthening public confidence in the Authority.

items.title: Diaspora nigérienne à Los Angeles : AFRIKICKS mène des forages, don majeur et annonces de projets structurants…
items.description: Un ressortissant nigérien établi à Los Angeles, dirigeant de l’ONG AFRIKICKS, a financé entre janvier 2023 et mai 2026 une série d’opérations de forages et effectué un don significatif afin de renforcer l’accès à l’eau potable et soutenir les autorités nigériennes, selon un bilan rendu public. AFRIKICKS, ONG dirigée par un compatriote installé aux États‑Unis, se donne pour mission « d’apporter une aide aux hommes, aux femmes et aux enfants à travers le monde en collectant des chaussures neuves et en bon état auprès de sympathisants aux États‑Unis ». Au Niger, l’organisation élargit son action sociale en projetant et finançant des forages de puits destinés à garantir l’accès à l’eau potable et à accompagner les autorités nationales dans leurs efforts de développement hydraulique. Bilan des forages (janvier 2023 – juin 2026) Le rapport compile les interventions réalisées dans des localités urbaines et rurales, ciblant principalement des écoles, des lieux de culte, des quartiers populaires et des villages à forte vulnérabilité hydraulique. Les opérations relevées sont entre autres : 25 janvier 2023, Quartier Talladjé — forage réalisé. 9 janvier 2024, Village de Guillaré — forage réalisé. 12 septembre 2024, Village de Bilfouda — forage réalisé. 19 septembre 2024, Quartier Pays Bas — forage réalisé. 4 juin 2025, Village de N’Dounga Saney — forage réalisé. 13 juin 2025, Quartier Yaboni Plateau — forage réalisé. 25 juin 2025, Groupe École Ballaré 8 (Aéroport) — forage réalisé. Septembre 2025, Village de Batako — forage réalisé. Septembre 2025, Village de Batoko Peulh — forage réalisé. 26 octobre 2025, Village de Bilfouda — forage réalisé. 2 novembre 2025, Village de Koné Beri, Gawado — forage réalisé. 7 novembre 2025, École primaire Rhodésie 3 — forage réalisé. 12 novembre 2025, Quartier Aéroport — forage réalisé. Novembre 2025, Mosquée Aéroport — forage réalisé. Mars 2026, Village de Delewa, CR N’Dounga — forage réalisé. Mai 2026, Village de Bazai Koira, CR Namaro — forage réalisé. Le 19 juin 2023, l’opérateur a remis un conteneur de 40 pieds d’une valeur estimée à 301 475 320 francs CFA au Fonds de Solidarité Pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie, don qualifié d’« exceptionnel » dans le rapport. Durant et après le Forum de la diaspora, organisé par le Gouvernement du Niger les 29 et 30 juillet 2026, plusieurs membres de la TEAM USA, basés aux États-Unis, ont présenté des projets structurants aux différentes agences gouvernementales, afin de contribuer à notre combat commun pour un Niger nouveau. Nous reviendrons plus en détail sur ces différents projets. Les axes identifiés couvrent : la finance et les investissements immobiliers ; les investissements pétroliers ; le transport routier à grande échelle ; la politique stratégique et la gouvernance ; la politique environnementale et le développement durable ; l’analyse de sécurité et la gestion de projet ; les réseaux mondiaux dans le domaine de l’éducation; recherche en parasitologie, biologie et pathologie humaine. Les participants du forum et des membres de la diaspora jugent ces compétences et initiatives comme « une nouvelle forme d’ouverture pour le Niger » et un apport concret à la refondation du pays, en proposant à la fois expertise, réseaux et opportunités d’investissement. Pour rappel, le renforcement de l’accès à l’eau constitue un enjeu majeur au Niger, où l’insuffisance des infrastructures hydrauliques impacte la santé, l’éducation et la résilience des communautés. Par Tamtaminfo News L’article Diaspora nigérienne à Los Angeles : AFRIKICKS mène des forages, don majeur et annonces de projets structurants… est apparu en premier sur Tamtaminfo .

items.title: « Dites à nos parents que nous allons bien », dixit les Appelés de la Tapoa
items.description: « Dites à nos parents que nous allons bien », dixit les Appelés de la Tapoa Diapaga, 13 août 2026 (AIB)- « Dites à nos parents que nous allons bien. Ici, on apprend à devenir des hommes et des femmes utiles pour le Burkina Faso », ont confié ce jeudi les Appelés de l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire de la Tapoa, à des journalistes venus prendre connaissance de leurs conditions d’apprentissage et de formation. Les médias locaux de la Tapoa ont effectué, ce jeudi 13 août 2026, une immersion médiatique dans le quotidien des appelés à l'immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO) sur le site de Diapaga. Cette journée des médias, faut-il le rappeler, est une initiative du camarade gouverneur de la région de l'Est, Ram Joseph Kanfando, en vue de donner plus de visibilité au vécu des appelés de la région dans leur site d'hébergement. Dans cette démarche, le camarade haut-commissaire de la Tapoa, président de la cellule provinciale de l'IPO, n'a pas ménagé ses efforts pour faciliter l'accès du centre aux médias. Il était accompagné, pour ce faire, du président de la Délégation spéciale de Diapaga, Yambi Bamogo. Face aux idées reçues et aux rumeurs circulant à l'extérieur, l'autorité régionale a bien voulu ouvrir les portes afin que les médias locaux touchent du doigt les réalités de ce centre. Il est 9h30 lorsque le cortège se présente devant la grande porte. À l'accueil, le sous-lieutenant Désiré Ilboudo, après les civilités, dresse son rapport. Le cortège est ensuite invité à intégrer le centre. Les appelés sonnent le rassemblement ; administration, encadreurs civils et militaires, ainsi que femmes conseillères, se retrouvent autour du camarade haut-commissaire pour le début de la cérémonie. S'adressant à l'assistance, le haut-commissaire déclare : « Aujourd'hui, nous ne faisons pas une visite de courtoisie, aujourd'hui nous faisons de la transparence. Cette journée des médias locaux, initiée par le camarade gouverneur de la région de l'Est, veut que les médias locaux voient de leurs propres yeux et touchent du doigt les réalités que vous vivez ici. » Il ajoute qu'on entend beaucoup de choses sur l'IPO : « Certains parlent de camps, d'autres de punition. Moi, je vous dis que l'IPO est une école. C'est l'école de la discipline, l'école du travail, l'école de la patrie. À vous, les journalistes, vous passerez quelques instants avec eux, à vivre leur quotidien, car pour raconter l'IPO, il faut la ressentir. Chers journalistes, vous avez une lourde responsabilité : celle de dire la vérité aux populations. Montrez que la jeunesse de l'Est n'a pas peur de l'effort, que la jeunesse de l'Est a choisi de répondre à l'appel de la RPP. » Il termine en invitant les appelés à être fiers et à parler vrai : « Montrez ce que vous avez appris. La région vous regarde, le Burkina vous suit. » À sa suite, le coordinateur du camp, le sous-lieutenant Désiré Ilboudo, a décliné le bilan à mi-parcours, livré les objectifs et évoqué les difficultés, avant de rappeler que l'IPO « ne forme pas des bras, elle forme des consciences ». Place a ensuite été donnée aux appelés, qui, à travers le délégué Tambaga Tankoano et son adjointe, Mme Ouoba, ont répondu aux questions de la presse. Les échanges ont porté sur l'image que les appelés avaient de l'IPO avant l'immersion, leur quotidien, les difficultés rencontrées, les motifs de fierté, les valeurs acquises et, enfin, leur message à l'endroit des jeunes n'ayant pas encore effectué l'IPO et de leurs parents. « Dites à nos parents que nous allons bien. Ici, on apprend à devenir des hommes et des femmes utiles pour le Burkina Faso », ont-ils confié. À l'issue des interviews, une visite guidée des locaux- infirmerie, administration, dortoirs, magasin des vivres, toilettes-a permis de mesurer le sérieux de l'organisation du centre. L'occasion a également été donnée au personnel administratif, aux encadreurs civils et militaires, aux agents de santé ainsi qu'aux femmes conseillères du site de présenter leurs missions respectives, ainsi que les difficultés auxquelles ils font face et la manière dont ils les surmontent, afin de former, au final, des appelés patriotes, responsables, disciplinés et profondément attachés à la nation. Au terme de cette journée des médias, Tambaga Tankoano et son adjointe ont lancé un appel vibrant à l'endroit des jeunes n'ayant pas encore effectué l'immersion : « Venez vivre l'IPO, c'est une école de la nation. C'est ici qu'on devient utile au Burkina. L'IPO forge, l'IPO transforme, l'IPO construit. Nous sommes la relève, nous sommes prêts pour la patrie. » Le constat est unanime : les appelés de la Tapoa se sont montrés fiers, disciplinés et heureux de l'esprit de corps qui les anime dans ce centre. Ils témoignent avoir vécu des moments exigeants, formateurs et patriotiques. Au terme de cette immersion, les journalistes retiennent des visages fiers, des cœurs heureux et des citoyens engagés : l'IPO se présente ainsi comme un véritable chemin de dignité. Agence d'information du Burkina LBK/ata

items.title: Colombie : le séisme pèse sur l'industrie du café et toute l'économie
items.description: Le tremblement de Terre qui a secoué la Colombie a été le plus meurtrier depuis le début du siècle et les dégâts matériels sont également considérables : 6,3 milliards de dollars au moins selon les premières estimations, l'équivalent de 1% du PIB du pays. L'industrie du café, pilier de l'économie du pays, est très impactée : la région d'Eje Cafetero est proche de l'épicentre, les infrastructures d'exportation des graines sont endommagées. Le café représente 3 à 4 milliards $ de revenus annuels.

items.title: Burkina/Vente d’oeufs de poulet: des commerçants pris en flagrant délit de pratiques frauduleuses
items.description: (Ouagadougou, le 13 août 2026) Une mission conjointe de la Brigade Mobile de Contrôle Économique et de Répression des Fraudes (BMCRF), de la Brigade Laabal, du service vétérinaire du Ministère de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau et des Ressources animales et halieutiques, ainsi que de la gendarmerie nationale, a été menée à la suite d’investigations sur le prix des œufs. Au cours de cette opération, plusieurs commerçants présumés auteurs de pratiques frauduleuses dont la spéculation et les pratiques de prix illicites ont été pris en flagrant délit. Les contrevenants ont été sanctionnés par des amendes et conduits par la Brigade Laabal pour effectuer des travaux d’intérêt commun. La BMCRF rappelle à l'ensemble des commerçants et aux consommateurs que le prix réglementaire des œufs est fixé à 3 000 F CFA la plaquette et 100 F CFA l’unité. Désormais, tout commerçant qui tentera de s’écarter de cette réglementation s’exposera à des amendes et à des travaux d’intérêt commun. 80 00 11 84/80 00 11 85/ 80 00 11 86 La BMCRF, la garantie d'une concurrence saine et loyale SCRP/BMCRF L’article Burkina/Vente d'oeufs de poulet: des commerçants pris en flagrant délit de pratiques frauduleuses est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Yadgar-i-Fatah monument inaugurated in Islamabad on eve of Independence Day
items.description: The Yadgar-i-Fatah monument, built to honour Pakistan’s martyrs and commemorate Marka-i-Haq , was inaugurated by President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad on Thursday night, on the eve of the country’s 80th Independence Day. President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmad Babar Sidhu and Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf were in attendance and stood for the national anthem, played by a military band. Foreign diplomats, military attaches, officers of the three services and other senior officials were also in attendance. (From L-R) Chief of Air Staff Air Marshal Zaheer Ahmad Babar Sidhu, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif attend the inauguration ceremony of the Yadgar-i-Fatah monument in Islamabad on August 13, 2026. — Screengrab via YouTube/ISPR Official ‘Guarantor of peace’ Addressing the ceremony, Prime Minister Shehbaz congratulated the nation on Independence Day and said that under Quaid-i-Azam’s leadership, “we entered the realm of freedom from the darkness of slavery. Our elders sacrificed their lives and property”. “Yadgar-i-Fatah symbolises our resolve and determination and the domination of our armed forces over the enemy,” he added. The premier also congratulated the nation on Marka-i-Haq and paid tribute to Field Marshal Munir for his leadership during the conflict, as well as Air Chief Marshal Sidhu and Admiral Ashraf. “Under his leadership, we defeated the enemy,” PM Shehbaz said. Paying tribute to the architects and engineers who designed the monument, the premier expressed appreciation for its sleek design and eight-month completion time. “Its completion in eight months would not have been possible if the field marshal hadn’t invested his deep interest,” PM Shehbaz added. “This is not just a monument of blocks, but a tribute to the martyrs who sacrificed their lives to defend the nation. That triumph is the victory of our army and our people, and this is our pride.” He noted that Pakistan wants peace, not war, and that desiring peace should not be perceived as a sign of weakness. “With dignity and determination, we are resolute for peace,” the premier stated, adding that Pakistan had been recognised as a “guarantor of peace” in the region. “If anyone challenges Pakistan’s sovereignty and defence, they will receive an even stronger reply than in May 2025,” he warned. PM Shehbaz noted that after suffering defeat, India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty unilaterally. “I warn that every drop of water is our red line. If India does not keep on the right track, we will give it a direct response,” he further warned. Speaking about the future of the country, PM Shehbaz recognised that doors needed to be opened for the younger generation. “We need to incorporate the latest technology to advance in the journey of our economic progress. We need to develop our human resources so our country will enter into a new phase of progress and well-being,” he stressed. “We must make a Pakistan where all provinces, including Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, will advance and develop together.” A world free of conflict The premier added that the nation wants to see a world “free from all sorts of conflict”. “We want to resolve all the issues with justice and in accordance with the UN Charter,” he emphasised, highlighting Islamabad’s role as a mediator between Iran and the US in the ongoing Middle East War. “The Makkah Agreement is the promise of peace for the Middle East, and a hope of peace for the Muslim world. It is also a message of peace for the whole world,” PM Shehbaz added. He further stated that Pakistan would keep advocating for the oppressed Palestinians and supporting their right to self-determination, while adding that Islamabad wants peace in Afghanistan, but the use of its soil for cross-border terrorism was “unacceptable”. “We need to stay united for peace and development. We need to bury the hate and revive the love for each other by forgetting our differences,” he emphasised. ‘We are not a small country to play with’ Taking the podium, President Zardari said that the nation and its armed forces, under Field Marshal Munir’s dynamic leadership, gave a befitting answer to India during the war last year. “This is in faith to remember what happened, in how many days it happened, where it happened, and this will go down in history for everyone to remember, whether today or the day after,” he said. He noted that Pakistan’s military response to Indian aggression demonstrated that “we are not a small country for you to play with”. “We are there as partners to the world, in the … family of countries,” President Zardari added. “And I think, today, even they understand that Pakistan is a national partner.” He added that the monument reflects the unity of the nation, the strength of the armed forces and the sacrifices given. The president recalled that his own father was called upon by Quaid-i-Azam to fight in the 1948 Kashmir War. “Most of Sindh, KP, other places, anybody who could carry an arm were there, and they fought against the Indian Army,” he stated. “By the grace of God, we got our Durand Line, our border line, but still so, a lot needs to be done … by us, the people and the public and definitely, the coming generation of Pakistan.” President Zardari noted that the premier, the CDF, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi were playing a “most commendable and praiseworthy” role. “We’ve been successful till now. Life comes and goes … we’ve seen tragedies, we’ve seen successes [and] successfully managed to guide our system through,” he added. “I’m not saying there would not be weaknesses; there always are; but there is no nation in the world that can claim they have no weaknesses.” Prior to the speeches by the country’s leadership, visuals broadcast on television showed a large contingent of personnel from the military, paramilitary forces and police presenting a guard of honour, accompanied by a military band. Personnel from the military, paramilitary forces and police present their standards during the inauguration ceremony of the Yadgar-i-Fatah monument in Islamabad on August 13, 2026. — Screengrab via YouTube/ISPR Official Yadgar-i-Fatah monument The marble monument was completed within eight months and features five archways, which represent the five pillars of Islam, as well as the five pillars of Pakistan itself — the government, the military, the media, the people and the ideology underpinning the nation. Additionally, they represent the three branches of the military — the Army, the Air Force and the Navy — as well as cyber-defence and space warfare. As part of the inauguration, a light and sound show was presented with moving images projected directly onto the monument, state television showed. One of the sequences highlighted the history of Pakistan and its military up until Marka-i-Haq . Iconic moments from the May war were also projected onto the monument, such as when villagers and Punjab Rangers shot at Indian drones together. Moving graphics are directly projected onto the Yadgar-i-Fatah monument during its inauguration ceremony in Islamabad on August 13, 2026. — Screengrab via YouTube/PTV News Following the light show, Pakistan Air Force fighter jets performed a flypast over the monument, deploying flares in the night sky. A Pakistan Air Force fighter jet performs a flypast over the Yadgar-i-Fatah monument in Islamabad on August 13, 2026. — Screengrab via YouTube/PTV News The monument marks Pakistan’s victory over India in a brief military conflict last May. The conflict with India — starting from the April 22 Pahalgam attack to the end of Operation Bunyanum Marsoos with a ceasefire between the two countries on May 10 — has been called “ Marka-i-Haq ” (Battle of Truth) by the state.

items.title: Gnagna : au Lycée provincial de Bogandé, 351 appelés plongés dans l’immersion patriotique
items.description: BURKINA-SIRBA-GNAGNA-IMMERSION PATRIOTIQUE Gnagna : au Lycée provincial de Bogandé, 351 appelés plongés dans l’immersion patriotique Bogandé, 13 août 2026 (AIB) – Quelque 351 jeunes appelés, dont 201 filles, prennent part depuis le 27 juillet 2026 à l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO) au Lycée provincial de Bogandé (LPB). Installés sur un site spécialement aménagé pour leur hébergement et leur formation, ils sont soumis à un programme axé sur le patriotisme, la discipline, le civisme et la vie communautaire. À leur arrivée, les appelés ont découvert un dispositif spécialement aménagé pour répondre aux besoins de leur séjour. Le site dispose notamment d’infrastructures dédiées à l’hébergement ainsi que d’un espace aménagé en amphithéâtre, servant de cadre aux cours, aux séances d’instruction et aux différentes activités de formation. L’organisation de l’IPO est assurée par un comité provincial présidé par le haut-commissaire de la Gnagna. Le secrétaire général de la province, Mendien dit Moussa Soma, rencontré sur le site, a indiqué que l’immersion patriotique vise notamment à renforcer chez les jeunes l’esprit patriotique, le sens de la responsabilité et l’engagement au service de la Nation. Selon lui, cette initiative doit permettre aux appelés de mieux prendre conscience de leurs responsabilités en tant que citoyens et de devenir des acteurs de la cohésion sociale et du développement de leurs communautés. Une formation fondée sur le patriotisme et la discipline Au quotidien, les appelés sont soumis à un programme d’activités combinant enseignements, séances d’instruction et exercices de vie collective. L’officier Sandaogo Ramdé du BIR 19, chargé de l’encadrement, a expliqué que les participants sont « rigoureusement soumis aux exigences du site d’immersion », conformément aux objectifs assignés à l’IPO. À travers cet encadrement, il s’agit, selon lui, de contribuer à la transformation des jeunes en citoyens patriotes, responsables et engagés. Les encadreurs mettent ainsi l’accent sur la discipline, le respect, le civisme, la solidarité, le vivre-ensemble et l’amour de la patrie. L’apprentissage ne se limite toutefois pas aux cours théoriques. La vie sur le site constitue également un cadre d’apprentissage de la vie en communauté. Les appelés doivent y respecter des règles communes et apprendre à cohabiter avec des jeunes issus de milieux et d’horizons différents. Une expérience de vie collective Pour les bénéficiaires, l’immersion patriotique constitue une expérience nouvelle, marquée à la fois par les exigences de la formation et par la découverte de la vie en collectivité. L’appelé Lihantipo Lankoandé apprécie particulièrement cette dimension communautaire. « C’est une expérience que nous vivons ensemble avec les autres », a-t-il souligné, mettant en avant les enseignements qu’il tire de cette cohabitation. Une jeune appelée relève, elle aussi, que la vie en communauté permet de dépasser les différences entre les participants. Malgré les divergences qui peuvent exister entre eux, « nous vivons en parfaite symbiose », affirme-t-elle, évoquant un climat fondé sur la cohésion sociale et la solidarité. Cette cohabitation quotidienne constitue ainsi l’un des piliers de l’IPO. Elle offre aux appelés l’occasion de mettre en pratique les valeurs de tolérance, de solidarité et de vivre-ensemble qui leur sont enseignées. Un dispositif attentif aux besoins des appelés Le caractère inclusif du dispositif se traduit également par la prise en compte des situations particulières de certains participants. Des femmes enceintes figurent notamment parmi les appelées accueillies sur le site de Bogandé. Celles-ci bénéficient d’une prise en charge adaptée, assurée par un professionnel du corps des sapeurs-pompiers affecté au site, afin de veiller à un accompagnement durant leur séjour. Au-delà des cours dispensés dans l’espace aménagé à cet effet, l’IPO au Lycée provincial de Bogandé se présente donc comme une véritable expérience de vie collective. Formation, discipline, encadrement et cohabitation constituent les principaux ressorts de ce séjour destiné à renforcer le sentiment d’appartenance à la Nation. Avec ses 351 appelés, dont 201 filles, le site de Bogandé constitue ainsi un cadre d’apprentissage où les jeunes sont invités à conjuguer patriotisme, citoyenneté, responsabilité et solidarité, dans la perspective d’une participation accrue à la construction et à la cohésion de la communauté nationale. Agence d’information du Burkina ayt/ata

items.title: Italie : explosion dans une usine de munitions
items.description: Une explosion s’est produite jeudi 13 août, en début d’après-midi, dans une usine de munitions située à Colleferro, à environ 40 kilomètres au sud-est de Rome. L’établissement, ancienne usine Simmel Difesa, appartient aujourd’hui à KNDS Ammo Italy, filiale du groupe de défense KNDS. L’usine produit notamment des munitions de moyen et gros calibre destinées à la défense terrestre et navale, ainsi que des combustibles solides pour les lanceurs aérospatiaux. L’explosion serait survenue dans le secteur de la compression des poudres. Selon les informations disponibles, aucune victime n’est à déplorer. Une vingtaine d’employés environ se trouvaient sur le site au moment des faits et aucun n’a été blessé. Des dégâts matériels, notamment des vitres brisées dans certaines habitations, ont toutefois été signalés. L’explosion a été précédée d’un incendie, permettant aux employés de se mettre à l’abri avant la déflagration. Selon les premiers éléments rapportés par la presse italienne, le feu pourrait être parti du secteur de la compression des poudres. Les pompiers et les carabiniers sont intervenus pour sécuriser le site. Des habitants de Colleferro ont filmé la scène, dont les images montrent la puissance de l’explosion. Une enquête a été ouverte par le parquet de Velletri afin de déterminer les circonstances et l’origine de l’incendie. La piste d’un incendie volontaire est notamment examinée. L’usine avait déjà été touchée par une explosion en octobre 2007, qui avait fait un mort et 13 blessés parmi les travailleurs. Tia DIAGNE
